question: Does the sentiment score lead, coincide with, or lag price?
method: Hourly change in average_compound vs hourly log return (Coinbase SYMBOL-USD candles), cross-correlation at offsets -12h..+12h. Positive offset = price moves after sentiment (sentiment leads). Significance uses a Bonferroni-corrected threshold across all 25 offsets. Only readings scored by the whole-word headline matcher (2026-10-03 on) are used. Script: scripts/leadlag.py --whole-word-only.
honest_prior: Scored from published news headlines, so the expectation is coincident-to-lagging. Results will be published here whatever they show.

methodology_changes.change: Headline matching changed from a substring test to whole-word, case-insensitive matching of the ticker, the coin name and per-coin aliases (for example "Ether" for ETH). Tickers that are ordinary words (LINK, DOT, NEAR, PUMP, HYPE, TAO) count only as "$TICKER" or by name, and HTML tags in feed descriptions are ignored when matching.
methodology_changes.before: Readings before 2026-10-03, and any made that day before the change was deployed, used substring matching, which counted words like "whether", "Tether" and "together" as ETH and "solution" as SOL. In a 224-headline sample on 2026-10-03, 16 of 47 ETH matches, 8 of 63 BTC, 8 of 15 SOL and 8 of 9 LINK were false.
methodology_changes.effect_on_validation: Hourly readings now record which matcher produced them. Lead/lag results are computed only from whole-word readings (scripts/leadlag.py --whole-word-only), so the two methods are never mixed in one window. First results are expected 14 days after the change is deployed.
methodology_changes.applies_to: Every score: on-demand calls, alerts, the hourly log and the daily dataset.
